title: Opening: Scripture sufficiently contains all that belongs to faith and salvation
source_text: I. Ecclesiarum, quae secessionem ab Ecclesia Romana fecerunt superiori saeculo, constans sententia est, Scripturam sacram, omnia quae ad fidem & salutem pertinent, sufficienter continere: ita ut opus non sit alio Dei verbo, unde ea, quae desunt Scripturae, suppleantur. Ecclesiae vero Romanae Doctores & propugnatores sententiam illam acerrime impugnant, estque ea de re gravis controversia, quam hisce thesibus & sequentibus aliquot tractare aggredimur. Ut autem distinctius & clarius id fiat, Ecclesiarum nostrarum sententiam quam dilucide & distincte a nobis fieri poterit exponemus. Deinde inquiremus in sententiam adversariorum, illamque cum nostra conferentes, manifestum reddemus quid proprie sit illud quod in quaestione est. Ac denique veritatem paucis confirmabimus, & adversae sententiae fundamenta subruemus.
pass_a_gloss: Of the Churches which made a secession from the Roman Church in the last century, the constant opinion is that sacred Scripture sufficiently contains all things which pertain to faith and salvation: so that there is no need of another word of God from which those things which are wanting to Scripture may be supplied. But the Doctors and champions of the Roman Church most sharply attack that opinion, and there is a grave controversy about this matter, which we undertake to treat in these theses and in some that follow. But in order that this may be done more distinctly and more clearly, we will set forth the opinion of our Churches as lucidly and distinctly as can be done by us. Then we will inquire into the opinion of the adversaries, and comparing it with ours we will make plain what properly is that which is in question. And finally we will briefly confirm the truth, and will undermine the foundations of the adverse opinion.
pass_b_english: The Churches that left Rome in the last century hold this steadily: sacred Scripture sufficiently contains everything that belongs to faith and salvation — so that we do not need another word of God to fill what Scripture supposedly lacks.
Rome’s doctors and champions attack that claim fiercely. The dispute is serious; we take it up in these theses and a few that follow.

For clarity we will first state our Churches’ view as plainly as we can, then compare the adversaries’ view with ours so the real question stands out, and finally confirm the truth briefly and undercut the opposite case.

choices.why: Historical Reformed departure from Rome, not modern schism sneer.
